lens: I refereed this as a journal referee would: safety and clinical language first for oligonucleotides that have never been synthesised, then whether the central claim survives the methods, whether the paper admits what it did not do, and whether I could reproduce the selection from what is in front of me.
what_i_read: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf (text extracted; sha256 of built_from source matches the pinned .md exactly)
research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv (data rows and the full # header block)
central_claim: Across 38 in-frame NR4A3 fusion junctions, junction-spanning 5-6-5 gapmers are designable everywhere but discrimination from the parent genes is the real constraint: roughly half the 190-design panel lets a mature wild-type parent pair its whole catalytic gap, so the paper names two specific research-use-only 16-mers at the two most-reported breakpoints that clear that screen, two screened scramble controls, five candidate test articles, and a pre-registrable selectivity threshold with its power and its void condition. It claims no efficacy, no delivery, no safety and no clinical readiness for any sequence.

blockers.summary: The only quantitative evidence that the two reagents named for synthesis clear the energy-based off-target screen is quoted as a bare point value, with none of the one-directional bias its producing artifact records - while every other bound in the paper carries its direction explicitly.
blockers.quote: Re-scored on duplex stability rather than on mismatch count, 8 designs carry a fully paired sixteen-base-pair off-target duplex and 45 one inside 2 kcal/mol of their own; neither named reagent is in either class, the closest to each being 3.2 and 3.0 kcal/mol weaker.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json is the source of those values (named_reagents.EWSR1_e12__NR4A3_e3.closest_gap_paired_ddg_1dp = 3.2; named_reagents.TAF15_e6__NR4A3_e3.closest_gap_paired_ddg_1dp = 3.0; summary.n_designs_with_a_fully_paired_offtarget_duplex = 8; summary.n_designs_with_a_gap_paired_near_match_within_2_kcal = 45). The same artifact carries three warning fields the manuscript does not reproduce anywhere: field '⚠_the_bound_runs_one_way' = 'Scoring only the longest perfectly paired run ignores pairing either side of a mismatch, so it UNDERSTATES a near-match's true stability and therefore OVERSTATES its separation from the intended duplex'; field '⚠_lna_not_modelled' = 'The table is for an unmodified DNA:RNA hybrid'; field '⚠_and_the_two_bounds_point_opposite_ways' = 'They are not a range and must not be quoted as one.' The manuscript's Methods (pinned .md line 125-127) states the metric ('re-scored on the nearest-neighbour stability of its longest contiguous paired run ... and only separations are reported') but never its direction. grep for kcal|energ|stabilit|understat|overstat over the pinned .md returns no such caveat, and the same grep over research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-supplementary-information.md returns nothing at all.
blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: The paper defines its own concern band as 2 kcal/mol and then reports the two named reagents as sitting 3.2 and 3.0 kcal/mol clear of it - a margin of only 1.0 to 1.2 kcal/mol above the band. Its own source says that margin is systematically inflated by an amount it explicitly declines to bound, and that the offsetting LNA bias must not be combined with it into a range. A reader deciding whether to synthesise these two molecules would conclude they clear the energy screen comfortably; the artifact does not support that conclusion at face value, and the paper carries the analogous directional caveat for every other bound it reports - the ten-base-pair cut ('adopted rather than measured'), the count of 87 ('bound the fully-paired class, not the whole parent liability'), the coverage figure ('an upper bound rather than an estimate'), the mismatch ceiling ('may under-call for reagents of this locked content'), the melting-point separation ('as a floor'), the panel counts ('a floor over that subset'), the allele screen ('bounds its class from below'). The single place the direction is dropped is the number that clears the two molecules the paper names.

p1s.summary: Every load-bearing number in the Abstract and Results is hand-typed prose restating a value that Tables 1 and 2 draw from the canonical CSV by generation. A regeneration of the screens would move the tables and leave the prose behind, and nothing in the document links them.
p1s.evidence: The manuscript's own front matter states the arrangement: 'the numbers live in the artifacts under research/modalities/ and are restated here where the argument needs them'. Table 1's caption in research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-tables.md states the opposite property for the tables - 'generated from the canonical sequence file so that a cell and its source cannot diverge' - which is precisely the guarantee the prose does not have. The exposed pairs I verified by hand today, each of which currently agrees: Abstract and Results 'eight and nine base pairs' against fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv column mature_parent_duplex_through_gap_bp = 8 and 9 for GGGCATATCATCAAAC and GGGCATATCTTGTGTG; Table 1's '≥ 26.6' and '≥ 36.0' against predicted_tm_fusion_c minus predicted_tm_best_parent_c (51.3-24.7 and 60.7-24.7); Results '123 ... against eight' against aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json named_reagents.*.n_gap_paired_scored; Results '3.2 and 3.0 kcal/mol' against closest_gap_paired_ddg_1dp; Results '68.4%' and '79.0%', which are derived products of PMID 36948401 (46/58 EWSR1, 9/58 TAF15) and PMID 12378528 (10/15 and 2/15 EWSR1 exon spans, 3/3 TAF15 exon 6) and appear nowhere as a stored field; Abstract '190', '38', '87', '61', '45.8%', '40.6%' against aso-parent-gap-pairing.json and aso-parent-null.json.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Re-running any screen and regenerating fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv - for instance after correcting a transcript model, changing the search ceiling, or adding a partner gene. Tables 1 and 2 would rebuild with the new values and the Abstract, the reagents paragraph and the panel paragraph would silently keep the old ones, leaving the paper internally contradictory in the two places a referee reads first. The same edit would also break the derived 68.4% and 79.0%, which no artifact stores and which therefore cannot be regenerated at all.

p2s.summary: The pre-registered selectivity endpoint may not be measurable in the only test articles that carry the named reagents' junctions, and the paper never says what would supply the wild-type NR4A3 arm or what readout separates the two transcripts.
p2s.evidence: Discussion defines the endpoint as 'the ratio of two half-maximal knockdown concentrations: wild-type NR4A3 over the fusion, from a matched dose-response in the same wells' - a within-well comparison of two transcripts. The Test articles section says the only two articles carrying the named reagents' junctions, E-N and T-N*, are engineered constructs and that 'a complementary DNA over-expressed in a heterologous background speaks to junction-selective knockdown of the intended transcript, not to activity at an endogenous locus'; PubMed's record for PMID 31020999 (doi:10.1002/path.5284) describes them as 'in vitro cell models engineered to ectopically express EWSR1-NR4A3 or TAF15-NR4A3'. The two models that would carry an endogenous wild-type NR4A3 allele, USZ20-EMC1 and USZ22-EMC2 (PMID 36316541), are reported at an exon-2 acceptor and the paper states they 'match different designs'. The manuscript nowhere states whether the heterologous host expresses wild-type NR4A3 at a level that supports an IC50, nor names an assay that distinguishes wild-type NR4A3 from the fusion in the same wells (for an exon-3 acceptor the only wild-type-unique sequence is NR4A3 exons 1-2). The stated limitation covers the fusion arm, not the wild-type arm. Adding one paragraph mapping each of the five test articles to which arm of the ratio it can supply would close this.

p2s.summary: Methods does not disclose that the first screen excludes the design's own parent genes by name and accession, so the reported transcriptome loads are not what a reader takes them to be.
p2s.evidence: Methods says only 'The first aligns against human RefSeq RNA, classifying each near-match by whether the catalytic gap is paired.' research/modalities/junction-aso-offtarget-e12n3-deep500-b1.json field method.parent_set records names_excluded = ['EWSR1','EWS RNA','NR4A3','NOR-1','nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 3'] and accessions_excluded = ['NM_005243','NM_006981']; research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json field _why states the same ('the alignment screen filters at >=14/16 identity and excludes parent records'), which is the stated reason the fourth screen exists. The headline 'Predicted transcriptome load separates the two: 123 gap-paired sense-strand near-matches for the EWSR1 reagent ... against eight for the TAF15 one' is computed after those exclusions, and the exclusion lists differ between the two reagents (EWSR1+NR4A3 versus TAF15+NR4A3), so the two loads are not compared on identical terms. In the manuscript this surfaces only obliquely in Results, as 'excluded by name rather than by that threshold'. One clause in Methods fixes it.

p2s.summary: The paper holds an arithmetic figure for the partial parent pairing at the NR4A3 exon-2/exon-3 seam of both named reagents and reports it as unmeasured.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript: 'Both also pair a wild-type parent through part of the gap at the NR4A3 exon-2/exon-3 seam their acceptor halves share, neither in full; those partial duplexes are not counted here and have not been measured.' research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv carries, for both GGGCATATCATCAAAC and GGGCATATCTTGTGTG, parent_paired_gap_dna_nt = 3 and parent_seam_hybrid_bp = 8; the file's own header defines these as 'ARITHMETIC on the design's OWN seam: gap nucleotides one of its own two parents pairs by construction. Not a search result' and 'that run plus the LNA wing beside it'. 'Not a search result' makes 'have not been measured' defensible in the narrow sense, but the assertion that the reagents pair 'through part of the gap ... neither in full' is itself derived from the 3-of-6 figure, and an 8 bp arithmetic floor on both named reagents sits in the very file the Declarations tell a reader to order from. The header also warns that this is confusable with the searched value ('For the lead 16-mer the first and third both read 8, from DIFFERENT genes, so a wrong join looks right on that design'), so if the number is being withheld deliberately, say that rather than 'have not been measured'.

p2s.summary: The Methods name no transcript accession, no Ensembl release and no value for the deeper search ceiling, so the selection cannot be reproduced from the article alone - in a paper whose predecessor was withdrawn for an exon-indexing error.
p2s.evidence: Methods says only 'Canonical transcripts for the five partner genes, and for NR4A3, were obtained from Ensembl'. The accessions exist in the artifacts: research/modalities/aso-premrna-offtarget.json genes.*.transcript = ENST00000397938 (EWSR1), ENST00000254108 (FUS), ENST00000395097 (NR4A3), ENST00000605844 (TAF15), ENST00000333725 (TCF12), ENST00000240851 (TFG). No release number appears in either place. Since 'Exon numbers throughout are transcript exon indices counted from the transcript 5' end, including non-coding exons' and 'an acceptor exon number read under the coding-exon convention instead selects a different reagent', an exon label without its transcript is not defined - which is the exact failure class the Data availability statement records as having caused a full withdrawal. Separately, the headline 'at a deeper search ceiling than the default' never names either ceiling; the artifacts encode it in filenames (deep500). The reagent sequences themselves are unambiguous, so nothing unsafe follows; this is reproducibility only.

p2s.summary: A documented class hazard of high-affinity LNA gapmers is presented as an adopted premise rather than a retrieved finding, and both named reagents sit in the chemistry that carries it.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript: 'High affinity is taken to carry a risk of sequence-dependent hepatotoxicity; that is a premise adopted here rather than a retrieved finding, and nothing here measures it.' This sits immediately after the paper establishes that both reagents carry five contiguous locked residues per wing - 'a high locked content against the two to four per wing taken here as usual' - and that both begin 5'-GGG, 'a contiguous locked G-tract'. Everywhere else the adopted-versus-retrieved convention makes a claim weaker; here it makes a safety statement weaker than the literature would. Retrieving and citing the LNA-gapmer hepatotoxicity literature would convert the paper's most substantive chemistry hazard from an assumption into a referenced finding at no cost to any claim.

p2s.summary: The framework's first step includes a transcriptomics component that none of the five screens performs, and the Abstract's phrasing does not make that clear.
p2s.evidence: Abstract: 'This work is computational, executing an industry off-target framework's in-silico step'. PubMed's record for PMID 39912803 (doi:10.1089/nat.2024.0072) states step 1 as 'OffT identification through complementarity prediction and transcriptomics analysis'. All five screens described in Methods are sequence searches over RefSeq RNA, unspliced parent sequence and GRCh38; no expression or transcriptomic data enters any of them, so no off-target is filtered or ranked by tissue expression. The Introduction's 'performs the in-silico half of the first step' is the only hedge, and 'half' is ambiguous because the whole of step 1 is in silico. One explicit sentence - no expression data were used, so off-targets are unweighted by tissue context - would settle it.

p2s.summary: The stated scope of the panel-count caveat is wider than the caveat it introduces, which invites a reader to discount counts it does not apply to.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript: 'Two bounds apply to every panel count below. First, seven of the 190 screens never returned, and the alignment screen censors the rest, leaving 47 of 183 assessable at all - so a count of clean designs is a floor over that subset, not a total over the panel.' The bound as stated in its own second clause applies to counts of CLEAN designs. The counts that immediately follow it - 87 liable, 61 against wild-type NR4A3, 85 by a design's own parent - are over the full 190 and are unaffected: research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json corpus.n_designs = 190, corpus.n_with_parent_duplex_through_gap = 87, corpus.which_parent_supplies_it.NR4A3 = 61, and I recomputed 85 from the per_design array. Narrowing 'every panel count below' to 'every count of clean designs below' removes the ambiguity.

p2s.summary: For the record: everything I could check reproduced exactly, which is worth stating because it is what makes the two omissions above conspicuous rather than routine.
p2s.evidence: Verified against the committed artifacts and recomputed where derived: 190 designs / 38 junctions / 87 liable / 61 against NR4A3 / 85 by own parent / max 13 bp (aso-parent-gap-pairing.json); 19 precursor-liable (aso-premrna-offtarget.json corpus.with_hybridisable_gap_paired); 8 fully-paired and 45 within 2 kcal (aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json summary); 176 distinct panel sequences and 9 tiled at more than one junction (fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv, 5-6-5 16-mers at NR4A3_e3); Table 1's ΔTm floors 26.6 and 36.0 as differences of the CSV's Tm columns; the whole cut ladder (35/31/23/9/6 junctions and 5/3/2/0/0 published ones at 10/9/8/7/6 bp, and 175 at seven and 181 at six designs) against aso-parent-null.json cut_sensitivity. I recomputed the null claims: 6.2% is the weakest of exactly ten ensembles, 40.6% is the strongest at ten, 91.4% against 92.1% at seven, the strongest null falls inside the panel's Wilson interval at every cut from seven to thirteen except eleven (checked all eight), and the excess over the strongest null changes sign exactly four times across cuts six to thirteen. I recomputed the statistics by Monte Carlo: at sd 0.35 on the log scale against a true selectivity of 3, the t-interval power is 30.4% at three replicates and 81.3% at six ('about 30%' and 'about 80%'), and the void thresholds solve to 0.6479, 1.5336 and 2.2498 for three, six and ten replicates ('about 0.65', '1.53', '2.25'). The normal-approximation caveat is real (72.8% and 92.7%). I recomputed 68.4% and 79.0% from PMID 36948401 (46/58 and 9/58) and PMID 12378528 (10/15, 2/15, 3/3) and both land exactly. All ten PMIDs I fetched from PubMed match their reference-list entries in author, year, journal, volume and pages. The PDF is built from the pinned .md byte-for-byte (build stamp sha256 209432ff... matches git show), carries 'Research use only - not for administration. Order from fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv, never from this PDF.' as a footer on every page, and repeats the full research-use-only statement in Declarations. The Zenodo DOI in Data availability is recorded as published and read back (research/manuscripts/aso/deposit-state.json published block). I found no efficacy, potency, tolerability, delivery, therapeutic-window or clinical-readiness claim anywhere in the document, and 'candidates' appears only in a negation.
